text:
Ethan Del Mastro is settling into the Blackhawks' blue line, as Bleacher Nation put it this week. He's a 23-year-old fourth-round pick playing about 13 minutes a night, with three assists in 13 games.

The interesting number is relative: Chicago gets 52% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, 12 points better than when he sits. On a team that has struggled to control play all season, that's a real contribution, even in a small sample.

He's also been unlucky. The Blackhawks have scored 6.3 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has kept his points down. His talent range expects a little more offense than he's shown.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, from six games last season, had him carrying the puck in on 46% of his entries and joining the rush more than most defensemen, but keeping possession on only 25% of his exits. What to watch: whether the strong on-ice numbers earn him more ice time on a team that needs it.
